title: Minimum Wage Australia: Converting Hourly to Annual Pay for 2026-27
description: Learn how to convert hourly rates to annual salary using the National Minimum Wage Australia. Includes tax, super, and casual loading estimates for 2026-27.
salarySummary: Based on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, the annual gross pay is approximately $52,269 before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the National Minimum Wage in Australia from 1 July 2026?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the formula is hourly × 38 × 52. The timesheet calculator on this site does this automatically.

faqs.q: Does the casual loading affect superannuation?
faqs.a: Yes, superannuation is calculated on your ordinary time earnings, which for casuals includes the casual loading. So super is 12% of your total ordinary earnings including loading, up to the maximum contribution base.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Annual Pay Formula

The basic formula to convert an hourly rate to an annual salary is: hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks. This assumes you work the same number of hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For full-time employees, the standard week is often 38 hours, as set by the National Employment Standards. For example, using the **minimum wage australia** from 1 July 2026 of $26.44 per hour, the annual gross pay is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,269.44 (rounded). If you are a casual employee, you receive a 25% casual loading on top of the base rate, making it $33.05 per hour, giving an annual gross of $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,336.80. This formula is the foundation of the [the timesheet](/) calculator on this site.

## The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, the rate is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. This is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. However, most Australian workers are covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates for their industry and classification. For example, the Hospitality Award or the Retail Award have specific rates for different roles. To find the correct rate for your job, you should check the relevant award via [pay guides](/blog) or the Fair Work Ombudsman. The National Minimum Wage is a floor, not a median. The Australian Bureau of Statistics' Average Weekly Earnings (May 2026) shows full-time adult ordinary time earnings at $2,083.70 per week – that is an average, not a median for any specific job. Your actual pay may differ.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on their base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave entitlements. This loading is included in the hourly rate you see in many job ads. When using the [the timesheet](/) calculator, you should enter the base hourly rate (without casual loading) and then check the "casual loading" box to add 25% on top. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading. Superannuation (super) is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Super is not deducted from your hourly rate; it is an additional cost to your employer. For a full-time employee on the National Minimum Wage, the annual super contribution would be approximately $52,269.44 × 12% = $6,272.33. For a casual employee, super is calculated on the total ordinary earnings including the casual loading, so $65,336.80 × 12% = $7,840.42. Note that if your earnings exceed the maximum contribution base, super is capped.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your gross annual pay is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office applies progressive tax rates for residents in 2026-27: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on income between $18,201 to $45,000, 30% on $45,001 to $135,000, 37% on $135,001 to $190,000, and 45% above $190,000. Additionally, a Medicare levy of 2% generally applies, with reductions for low-income earners (using 2025-26 reduction thresholds as 2026-27 thresholds were not confirmed). For a full-time worker on the National Minimum Wage ($52,269.44), the tax would be approximately: $0 on first $18,200, then 15% on $26,800 ($4,020), then 30% on $7,269.44 ($2,180.83) – total tax $6,200.83, plus Medicare $1,045.39 (2% of $52,269.44) = $7,246.22 total deductions, leaving take-home of about $45,023.22. This is an estimate; the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator on this site can give a more precise figure. Remember, this estimate does not include HELP repayments, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, divide your annual salary by 26. For the National Minimum Wage example: $52,269.44 ÷ 26 = $2,010.36 per fortnight. For a casual on the same base rate: $65,336.80 ÷ 26 = $2,512.95 per fortnight. This can help you budget and compare job offers that quote different pay periods.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

The [the timesheet](/) page is designed to help you convert your hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay, with tax and super estimates. Simply enter your base hourly rate, select your hours per week (default 38), and optionally check the casual loading box if applicable. The calculator will then show your annual gross, tax, Medicare, and net pay. It uses the same assumptions listed in the disclaimer: no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. It is a tool for estimation, not a determination of your pay. For award-specific rates, refer to the [pay guides](/blog) or [job pay](/topics/job-pay) pages.

## Conclusion

Understanding how to convert hourly to annual pay is essential when evaluating job offers. The National Minimum Wage Australia sets a baseline, but most workers earn more under an award. Always check your award rate and consider casual loading and super. Use the calculators on this site to get a personalised estimate of your take-home pay.
